 Starc’s three-word response as sandpaper villain threatens to break silence
 Simon Brunsdon November 16, 2026 - 8.26pm 
 Powered by shares Share article Cameron Bancroft is considering breaking his silence on the infamous Sandpapergate and a former teammate says “go for it”.
 Bancroft was the player caught by South African broadcast cameras with sandpaper in his pocket during the fateful 2018 Test in Cape Town.
 Cameron Bancroft and David Warner playing Test cricket in 2017.  AAP 
 Advertisement He was whacked with a nine-month ban from Cricket Australia and has only played twice for his country again, with his once-promising Test career appearing set to remain at only 10 matches forever.
 He was recalled to the Test side during the 2019 Ashes but has not featured since despite some phenomenal returns for Western Australia in the Sheffield Shield, and there are suggestions he has been blacklisted from selection following comments made in a 2021 interview where he insinuated the team’s bowlers knew of the illegal ball-tampering methods – a claim that has been refuted by all of Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, and Nathan Lyon.
 Now, in the wake of Usman Khawaja’s explosive allegations made in his newly released book , Bancroft’s manager revealed the 33-year-old is considering speaking publicly to give his side of the story.
 “He’s assessing whether he’ll put something out in the coming days,” Ben Tippett of Entourage Management told The Sydney Morning Herald and The Age .
 Khawaja’s bombshell suggestion that “everyone knew” about the ball-tampering in 2018 is a point of division in Aussie cricket.
 Read more
 ‘Weak leadership’ slammed as gap between sandpaper truth widens 
 Current captain Cummins gave a 70-minute press conference last week where he strongly denied he knew sandpaper was being used by his teammates to alter the condition of the ball, which assisted in the bowlers getting reverse swing.
 Former fast bowler Chadd Sayers, who was on the 2018 tour to South Africa, said on SEN he knew about the illegal methods being used , and he believed the other bowlers knew too.
 Advertisement Khawaja, Cummins, and David Warner have all made their positions clear but the sporting world is desperate to hear from the likes of Bancroft, Steve Smith, Starc, Hazlewood, and Lyon to get a better understanding of who knew what.
 Starc was flying to Kangaroo Island for a charity golf event on Monday and was stopped at the airport by 9News.
 When told Bancroft may speak about the saga Starc simply replied, “go for it”, and when asked whether Sayers was telling the truth he said, “you’ve got to ask Chadd that, don’t you”.
 Aussie cricket great Darren Lehmann, who was coach of the Test team when the scandal broke in 2018, hopes the furore can be put to bed as soon as possible.
 Advertisement Advertisement Mitchell Starc stopped by journalists.  Nine 
 “It’s been a tough week for everyone involved,” Lehmann told 9News.
 “We’ve got to try move forward for Australian cricket, but how that happens I don’t know… your guess is as good as mine.
 “Let’s see what happens over the next little while.”
 Advertisement While Australia is playing a white-ball series against England currently, the Test team’s next assignment begins December 9 against New Zealand in Perth.
 It will be their first match since Khawaja’s explosive claims were made public.
